title: Risotto Milanese
subtitle: Saffron risotto, the classic Milanese
excerpt: Arborio rice cooked slowly in white wine and hot stock, stirred constantly until creamy and al dente, then finished with saffron, butter, and Parmesan. The backbone of Milanese cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto alla milanese is the signature dish of Milan, traditionally served as an accompaniment to ossobuco. Its distinctive golden colour comes from saffron. The first recorded recipe dates from 1829. The technique that defines all risotto is the mantecatura: stirring cold butter and Parmesan into the cooked rice off the heat at the end, which gives the dish its characteristic creamy consistency. Properly made risotto should flow slowly and stretch into a wave when the plate is tilted.

recipeTools.notes: For the risotto. A wide, heavy-based pan is ideal.

content.text: Keep the stock at a gentle simmer in a separate pan throughout: cold stock shocks the rice and stops it cooking evenly. Add the stock a ladleful at a time and wait until each addition is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This is the technique that releases the starch and creates the creamy consistency. The mantecatura at the end, adding cold butter and Parmesan off the heat, is what binds it all together.
Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water. Keep the stock simmering in a separate pan.

Melt 40 g of butter in a wide, heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 5 minutes until very soft but not coloured. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are translucent at the edges.

Add the white wine. Stir until absorbed. Add the saffron with its soaking liquid. Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for about 18 to 20 minutes until the rice is al dente and the risotto is creamy.
Remove from the heat. Add the remaining cold butter and the Parmesan. Stir vigorously for 1 minute until glossy and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.
